from_quote: In my last number I endeavored to prove
rationale: The paragraph refers to Cato's "last number" and summarizes its subjects, which are those of Cato 4 (the executive, the ten miles square, the vice-president).
Among its objections "to the first article", the paragraph names the "biennial elections for representatives".

from_quote: that the number of representatives are too few ; that the apportionment and principles of increase are unjust
rationale: Among its objections "to the first article", the paragraph names the number of representatives and their apportionment and increase, which are set in Article I, Section 2, clause 3.

from_quote: that the mode in which they are appointed and their duration will lead to the establishment of an aristocracy
rationale: Among its objections "to the first article", the paragraph names the mode of appointing senators and their duration in office, set in Article I, Section 3, clause 1.

from_quote: that the senate and president are improperly connected, both as to appointments and the making of treaties
rationale: The paragraph names the joint part of the senate and president in appointments and treaties, set in Article II, Section 2, clause 2.
to_quote: by and with the Advice and Consent of the Senate

from_quote: the making of treaties, which are to become the supreme law of the land
rationale: The paragraph names the provision making treaties "the supreme law of the land".
to_quote: shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: as to the trial of impeachments, is placed in the senate
rationale: The paragraph names the provision placing "the trial of impeachments" in the senate.
to_quote: The Senate shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments

from_quote: that Congress have the improper power of making or altering the regulations prescribed by the different legislatures, respecting the time, place and manner of holding elections for representatives, and the time and manner of chosing senators
rationale: The paragraph describes in close wording the clause on the times, places and manner of holding elections, which Congress "may at any time by Law make or alter".
to_quote: the Congress may at any time by Law make or alter such Regulations

from_quote: that standing armies may be established, and appropriation of money made for their support for two years
rationale: The paragraph names the power to raise armies with appropriations for two years, from Article I, Section 8, clause 12.
to_quote: no Appropriation of Money to that Use shall be for a longer Term than two Years

from_quote: that the slave trade is, to all intents and purposes, permanently established
rationale: The paragraph names the slave trade among its objections to the first article; the only provision on it is the clause on the migration or importation of persons in Article I, Section 9.

from_quote: established biennial elections for the house of representatives, who are to be chosen by the people
rationale: The paragraph names the biennial election of the house of representatives by the people.
to_quote: chosen every second Year by the People of the several States

from_quote: sextennial for the senate, who are to be chosen by the legislatures of the different states
rationale: The paragraph names the six-year term of senators chosen by the state legislatures.
to_quote: chosen by the Legislature thereof, for six Years

from_quote: have given to the executive the unprecedented power of making temporary senators, in case of vacancies by resignation or otherwise
rationale: The paragraph names the provision for temporary appointments of senators by the executive "in case of vacancies by resignation or otherwise".
to_quote: if Vacancies happen by Resignation, or otherwise, during the Recess of the Legislature of any State, the Executive thereof may make temporary Appointments

from_quote: that six men can be a complete and full representation of the numbers and various orders of the people in this state
rationale: The paragraph refers to the six representatives allotted to New York until the first enumeration.
